title: Green tests, broken release
scenario: "Add a featured column to products." Unit tests pass in memory — but the SQL is wrong. (FEAT-04)
mission: Let the PostSync smoke catch a bad release in dev, keep prod untouched, roll back by revert and propose the missing integration test.
objectives: Explain unit vs integration vs smoke
Recover dev by reverting the deploy PR

prerequisites.notes: C011 done (the API really uses SQL).

steps.title: Ship the bad change
steps.detail: Select a non-existent column; tests stay green; merge; merge the dev deploy PR.

steps.title: Observe
steps.detail: Pods Ready? Smoke? Argo CD sync status?

steps.title: Roll back
steps.detail: Revert the dev deploy PR; do not promote.

steps.title: Fix forward
steps.detail: New branch with the fix and an integration test against SQL.

criteria.text: A failed smoke for the bad tag is visible in the dev sync history
Prod values never referenced the bad tag
Dev runs a tag whose smoke passed
An integration test that exercises the SQL path exists

expectedResult: A bad release stopped in dev with zero customer impact.

concepts.title: The test pyramid
concepts.body: *Unit* tests check logic in isolation (fast, many). *Integration* tests check a component with its real dependency (e.g. a SQL container). *Smoke* tests check a deployed environment answers end to end (few, slow). Each layer catches bugs the others miss.

concepts.title: Readiness vs smoke
concepts.body: A readiness probe answers "can this pod receive traffic?" — here it only pings the database. It does not run the product query. The PostSync smoke calls the real endpoint, so a wrong SQL column fails there.

example.title: an integration test with a real database in CI
example.body: GitHub Actions can start a database as a service container next to the job; tests then connect to it:
example.code:
services:
  sql:
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest
    env: { ACCEPT_EULA: "Y", MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CI_SQL_PASSWORD }} }
    ports: [ "1433:1433" ]

glossary.def: Ship a corrected version instead of reverting.
Health check deciding if a pod gets traffic.
Container started for the duration of a CI job.

recovery: If Argo CD keeps retrying, the revert has not merged yet — check the PR.
dont: Do not promote a release whose smoke failed
Do not use kubectl rollout undo
hints: /readyz only pings the database; /api/products runs the query.
The sync operation fails when a PostSync hook fails.
An integration test can run against a SQL container in CI.

interview.question: Your unit tests passed but production would have broken. What was missing in your test strategy?
followUps: Where do contract and integration tests run?

debrief: In-memory mode hid the SQL error from unit tests; readiness only pings the DB; the smoke exercised the real query and failed the sync. Rollback is a Git revert; the durable fix is an integration test in CI.

checker.plan: Read-only: Argo CD application history (kubectl get application -o json), git log of envs values, test file scan.
